title: Best AI Story Games 2026: 20 Tools to Play, Write, Build
summary: 20 AI story games and text adventure generators for 2026, sorted by what you get: an AI game master, a co-writer, or a game you publish. Free plans checked.
body_markdown:
An AI story game is a story you play by typing. You say what your character does, and an AI writes what happens next, so no two runs end the same way. In 2026 the category splits three ways: AI game masters you play in (AI Dungeon, Friends & Fables, Hidden Door), co-writers that help you steer the prose (NovelAI), and engines that let you build and publish your own interactive fiction (Twine, ink, Ren'Py). We checked the free plan of all 20 tools below on November 7, 2026, and we flag each page that did not load.


The hard part has not changed since Colossal Cave Adventure: a story game is only as good as its memory and its rules. A model that forgets your sword after twenty turns breaks the spell, and a game master with no rules lets you win every fight. So we sorted these tools by what they give you at the end of an evening, and by how well they keep the story straight.

Free plans checked November 7, 2026. Plan your plot first with the free[AI story game generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-story-generator) .

## What Is an AI Story Game?


**An AI story game is interactive fiction where a language model writes the next scene in response to anything the player types, instead of picking from branches an author wrote in advance.** Classic interactive fiction, such as Zork, Choice of Games titles and Twine stories, uses authored branches. AI story games generate the branch on demand, which is why you can try an action no writer planned for.


That one difference splits the category. A writer who builds a branching story in Twine knows every ending, because they wrote every ending. A player in AI Dungeon does not, and neither does the AI. A research team led by Mark Riedl described the hard version of the problem in the 2025 paper[Story2Game](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03547) : a model can draft a story, but a playable game also needs world state that tracks what each action requires and changes, so that a new action the player invents still obeys the world's logic.


So "AI story game" now means five different products. Each hands you something different at the end of an evening:



If you want a playable arcade, platformer or 3D game from a prompt rather than a story, see our guide to[AI game generators](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-game-generators) . This page covers the narrative side: text adventures, AI game masters, interactive fiction engines and the tools that plan a story before it is built.

## How an AI Game Master Runs a Turn


**Every turn, an AI game master reads your action, the recent story and any saved facts, then writes the next scene.** Saved facts are things like AI Dungeon story cards, a NovelAI lorebook entry or a Friends & Fables long-term memory. Platforms built on tabletop rules add one more step: they resolve the action against a rules engine, such as a combat turn, before they narrate the result.


Open-ended platforms such as AI Dungeon and Perchance skip the rules step and let the model decide what happens. That is why they feel free and surprising, and also why a determined player can talk their way past any obstacle. Friends & Fables keeps the rules step: its homepage describes "tactical turn-based combat based on D&D 5e rules," with battlemaps, spells and monsters. Neither approach is better. They are built for different evenings.


Memory works in three layers, and knowing them explains most of the frustration players report:


1. **The recent context.** The last stretch of the story that the model reads every turn. How much it can read depends on the model and, on several platforms, on your plan.
2. **Saved facts you write.** Story cards, lorebook entries and pinned notes. The platform injects them when a trigger word appears.
3. **Memories the platform writes.** Summaries and long-term memories the system saves on its own as the story goes on.


The same three layers show up in every AI agent, not only in games. Our[history of agent memory](https://www.taskade.com/blog/agent-memory-history) traces why models forget, and[the history of the context window](https://www.taskade.com/blog/context-window-history) shows how much recent text a model can read. If the idea of an AI that plans, remembers and acts is new, start with[what an AI agent is](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-are-ai-agents) . An AI game master is an agent with one job: keep the story going.

## Why AI Story Games Forget, and Which Tools Remember


**AI story games forget because a language model sees only a fixed amount of recent text, so early details fall out of view in a long run.** Tools fight this with saved facts, summaries and structured world state. Authored engines such as Twine never forget, because the writer stores every fact in a variable.

Three habits keep a long run straight on any platform:


- **Keep a "story so far" paragraph.** Every few sessions, ask the AI to summarize the plot, then paste that summary into a pinned note or story card.
- **Pin the facts that matter.** Names, items, promises and injuries belong in saved facts, not only in the chat history.
- **End a chapter on purpose.** Start a fresh run with a recap instead of pushing one story past several hundred turns.


The "Drift" state is where most AI story games lose players. A character you killed walks back in, or the AI forgets the quest you accepted. The tools that handle it best either keep world state outside the model (Altworld, Friends & Fables) or hand the player clear tools to pin facts (AI Dungeon story cards, NovelAI lorebooks). A "start a new chapter" habit works on every tool.

## How We Compared These Tools


**We grouped the 20 tools by what they produce, then checked each one's free plan, price, memory, export and rights on the vendor's own page on November 7, 2026.** A game master and a Twine editor are not competitors, so we did not rank them against each other.


We did not run an identical-prompt bake-off. Most platforms meter free turns, several put their stronger models behind paid plans, and story quality depends heavily on the player. A single prompt would have measured luck as much as quality. Instead we answered five questions for every tool:


Question What counts as a yes Where we looked


What do you get back? A clear output: a played story, prose, a game file or a plan Product pages


Can you play or make something on $0? A free plan, trial or free software that produces a result Pricing pages


Does it remember? A stated memory system: cards, lorebook, memories or variables Product pages and docs


Can you take it with you? An export, a file or a public link you control Product pages and docs


Can you sell it? A license or terms line that allows commercial use Terms, licenses and pricing


Where a vendor page did not load or did not publish a number, this post says "not published" or "not verified" and quotes no third-party figure. Every entry names at least one real strength, because every tool here is the right choice for someone. Taskade appears in the design group, because it is not an AI game master platform and does not compete on turn-by-turn play.

## Play: AI Game Masters and Text Adventures


These tools write the story with you, one turn at a time.


### 1.[AI Dungeon](https://aidungeon.com/) : Best Open-Ended Text Adventure


[AI Dungeon](https://aidungeon.com/) brought AI text adventures to a mass audience. Nick Walton built the first version at a hackathon in March 2019, and AI Dungeon 2 launched in December 2019 and passed 100,000 players within a week. Latitude now runs it alongside Voyage, its multiplayer story product, which opened to everyone in August 2026.


**Key features:** a large community library of scenarios; story cards that inject facts when a keyword appears; a memory bank; several AI models; public multiplayer through Voyage.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** the pricing FAQ says "You can use the model at this base amount endlessly without needing to spend anything," and "Voyage public multiplayer is free for everyone and does not require a subscription." The plan list itself did not load, so we do not quote free-tier limits.


**Pros:**


- The largest scenario library and community in the genre
- Free play has no stated turn cap on the base model
- Story cards give you real control over memory


**Cons:**


- Larger context and stronger models sit on paid tiers
- Long runs need steering to stay coherent


**Pricing:** paid memberships "include a monthly Credit allowance that refreshes each billing cycle," and credits do not expire. Tier prices were not visible on the vendor page on November 7, 2026.


**Bottom line:** the first stop for an open-ended text adventure tonight, especially if you like to write your own scenarios.


### 2.[Friends & Fables](https://fables.gg/) : Best AI Game Master for D&D-Style Campaigns


[Friends & Fables](https://fables.gg/) is an AI game master for tabletop-style campaigns. Its homepage promises "tactical turn-based combat based on D&D 5e rules," with battlemaps, spells, abilities and monsters, and it states that it is not affiliated with Wizards of the Coast. It says more than 100,000 players and world builders use it.


**Key features:** an AI game master that narrates and runs 5e-based combat; long-term memories on every plan; world-building tools such as map makers and character generators; parties of up to 6 players on the top plan; public and featured worlds.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "Up to 25 turns per day," "Long-term Memories," "Unlimited Campaign Slots," "Your friend can play for free," and "3 player campaigns."


**Pros:**


- Rules and combat instead of free-form narration
- Friends join your campaign for free
- Memories are included on Free, not saved for paid plans


**Cons:**


- 25 turns a day ends a long session early on Free
- Text to Speech starts on paid plans


**Pricing:** Starter $19.95/month (unlimited standard turns, 4-player campaigns), Pro $29.95/month, Legend $39.95/month. Yearly billing is advertised as "2 Months Free."


**Bottom line:** the best choice when you want an AI dungeon master that respects rules, especially for a group.


### 3.[Hidden Door](https://hiddendoor.co/) : Best for Stories in Worlds You Already Know


[Hidden Door](https://hiddendoor.co/) builds story games on licensed and classic worlds. Its homepage lists Dracula, The Land of Oz, The Call of Cthulhu, Pride & Prejudice, Sherlock Holmes and more. Creators model a world in Atlas, its world-building studio, and one world can feed "interactive fiction, character chat, social games, microdramas, comics, and audio series."


**Key features:** licensed and public-domain story worlds; play as your own character; character chat; profiles and achievements; content ratings per world, from All ages to Mature; a Creator MCP that lets you build worlds from AI assistants.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "Enjoy unlimited play across the whole catalog, free," with "Jump into any world, without limits."


**Pros:**


- Worlds with real authors and real canon behind them
- Unlimited free play across the catalog
- Content ratings help parents and teachers choose


**Cons:**


- The Creator tier price is not published
- You play inside worlds Hidden Door hosts, so open sandbox play is narrower


**Pricing:** a Creator tier for making and sharing worlds of your own, price not published. Accepted partners get Creator at no cost.


**Bottom line:** the best pick if you want to walk into Oz or Dracula's castle, not an empty fantasy map.


### 4.[NovelAI](https://novelai.net/) : Best Co-Writer for Prose and Style Control


[NovelAI](https://novelai.net/) is a writing tool first and a game second. Its tagline is "Write worlds that remember everything." Writers use it to draft fiction with tight control over style, and its Text Adventure mode turns the same editor into a game: a Do input adds "You" to the front of an action, and a Say input turns your line into dialogue.


**Key features:** a story editor with style controls; a Lorebook that loads facts when keywords appear; Text Adventure mode with Do, Say and Story inputs; image generation; text to speech.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** a Paper trial with "50 free Text generations," 30 image generations and 100 text-to-speech generations for an email-verified account. There is no permanent free plan.


**Pros:**


- The most control over prose in this list
- Lorebook is a mature, well-documented memory tool
- Its terms say you "retain all rights and ownership" of your content


**Cons:**


- The trial runs out fast in a long adventure
- It feels like a writing app, so players who want a game master may prefer AI Dungeon


**Pricing:** Tablet $10/month, Scroll $15/month, Opus $25/month.


**Bottom line:** the best fit for writers who want to steer every sentence, with adventure play as a bonus.


### 5.[FableAI](https://fableai.app/) : Best for Co-Op Stories With Voice


[FableAI](https://fableai.app/) is a story app built for playing together. Its tagline is "Live inside any story," and the site advertises "real-time multiplayer adventures across 5,000+ stories" on iOS, Android and the web. The mobile apps add voice narration and push notifications for multiplayer turns.


**Key features:** solo and real-time multiplayer stories; a large library of community stories; voice narration in the mobile apps; gems that unlock more play and faster responses.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "a forever-free plan and no credit card needed to start," with "Free plan, no time limit." Gems and optional subscriptions unlock more play.


**Pros:**


- Built around co-op play from the start
- Works in a browser and on both mobile platforms
- A forever-free plan with no card


**Cons:**


- Subscription and gem prices are not published on the site
- Gems cap how much you play on the free plan


**Pricing:** "Optional subscriptions and gem packs unlock more play, faster responses, and extra features." Prices appear only in the app. Link only` fableai.app` : the` fableai.io` domain is unrelated.


**Bottom line:** the best pick for a story night with friends on their phones.


### 6.[Perchance AI RPG](https://perchance.org/ai-rpg) : Best Free Text Adventure With No Sign-Up


[Perchance AI RPG](https://perchance.org/ai-rpg) is a free web page that runs a text adventure with no account. Its page title reads "AI RPG - Text Adventure - free, unlimited, no sign-up," and its description says it has no daily usage restrictions. Perchance is a platform of user-made generators, so several community versions exist, including an "Enhanced RPG" with a lorebook and story forking.


**Key features:** instant play in the browser; editable memory; saves in your browser's storage; community remixes of the generator with extra features.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** free, no sign-up, and no daily limit by the page's own description. The page body blocked our fetch, so we checked the title and description only.


**Pros:**


- Zero cost and zero friction
- Memory you can read and change yourself
- Community versions add lorebooks and branching


**Cons:**


- Saves live in one browser, so clearing it or switching devices loses a run
- Long runs drift, and there is no account to sync progress


**Pricing:** free.


**Bottom line:** the fastest way to try an AI text adventure, and a good test of whether you like the genre before you pay anyone.


### 7.[Altworld](https://altworld.io/) : Best for a Persistent World That Keeps State


[Altworld](https://altworld.io/) treats the world as data. Its site says the world "keeps state," and that "structured state (factions, rumors, prices, relationships) updates first," before the AI writes the scene. Runs are saved as you play, and you can return later or branch from an earlier point.


**Key features:** structured world state; saved runs and branching; guest play in the browser; daily Candles for free accounts.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "Your first 10 turns work as a guest with no account," and "Free accounts receive daily Candles that fuel continued play." Optional top-ups exist for long sessions.


**Pros:**


- World state lives outside the model, so facts drift less
- You can try 10 turns before you sign up
- Branching lets you replay a choice


**Cons:**


- Top-up prices are not on the homepage
- Altworld publishes its own "best of" list, like several vendors in this category


**Pricing:** daily Candles on a free account, with optional paid top-ups. The homepage lists no amounts.


**Bottom line:** a strong pick for players who care most about a world that remembers what they did.


### 8.[Character.AI](https://character.ai/) : Best for Talking to One Character, Not Running a Story


[Character.AI](https://character.ai/) is one of the largest character-chat platforms, and many players use it as a story game. It works best as a conversation with one character, not as a structured adventure with quests and endings. In late 2025 it removed open-ended chat for users under 18 and pointed teens to Stories, a guided format with choices.


**Key features:** a huge library of user-made characters; casual one-on-one chat; a guided Stories format with choices; a c.ai+ subscription.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** free to start with an account. Open-ended chat is for adults only since the late-2025 change.


**Pros:**


- One of the largest character libraries on the web
- Fast, casual, and easy to start
- Stories add structure for younger users


**Cons:**


- No rules, quests or endings in open chat
- No public pricing page, so the c.ai+ price is hard to check before you buy


**Pricing:** a c.ai+ subscription, sold in the app. We could not verify the price on a public Character.AI page on November 7, 2026.


**Bottom line:** the right choice when you want to talk to a character, and the wrong one when you want a story with stakes.

## General AI Assistants as a Free Game Master


A general AI assistant runs a decent text adventure if you give it a clear game-master prompt. The prompts section below has five to copy.


### 9.[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) : Fastest Way to Start a Chat Adventure


[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) is the assistant most people already have open, which makes it the fastest way to try a story game. Paste a game-master prompt, name a genre and a character, and it will narrate. Its memory feature can also carry preferences between chats, and the free plan includes limited memory and context.


**Key features:** chat with any genre or style; memory across chats, limited on Free; image creation for scenes; voice chat; projects that keep a campaign's files together.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "Unlimited text chats," with a footnote that they are "subject to abuse guardrails." Uploads, images, voice and memory are limited on Free.


**Pros:**


- No new account if you already use it
- Flexible enough for any genre, rule set or tone
- Images and voice add atmosphere


**Cons:**


- No built-in game rules, so you must police the game master
- The story lives in a chat thread, not a game you can share


**Pricing:** Go, Plus and Pro plans. The pricing page showed no dollar amounts on November 7, 2026.


**Bottom line:** the quickest free test of an AI game master, with the least structure.


### 10.[Claude](https://claude.ai/) : Best Free Assistant for Long Campaigns and Playable Story Artifacts


[Claude](https://claude.ai/) by Anthropic handles long, consistent campaigns well, and it can do something chat-only tools cannot: turn a story into a small playable artifact. Ask it for a branching story as a single HTML file, and you get a page with clickable choices that you can share by link. That is the same[single-file HTML](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-html-generators) pattern many browser games use.


**Key features:** long conversations; memory across conversations; artifacts that render playable HTML; projects that hold a campaign's notes; free plan access.


**Free plan (checked Nov 7, 2026):** "Free for everyone," with limited usage that resets every 5 hours and every week, and up to 5 projects.


**Pros:**


- Strong at keeping a long campaign's details consistent
- Artifacts turn a story into a playable page
- Projects keep a campaign's world notes in one place


**Cons:**


- Free usage limits interrupt long sessions
- No rules engine, so combat and items are on the honor system


**Pricing:** Pro $17/month billed annually ($200 up front) or $20 billed monthly. Max $100/month. Ultra $200/month.


**Bottom line:** the best free assistant for a story you want to turn into something other people can click through.


### 11.[SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) : Best Self-Hosted Option for Full Control


[SillyTavern](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern) is "a locally installed user interface that allows you to interact with text generation LLMs." It is the power-user front end of the story game world. ## How to Make Your Own AI Story Game in Five Steps


**You can make a playable story game in an afternoon if you plan the premise, the cast and the branch map before you write a single scene.** The five steps below work with any build tool, from Twine to a Taskade Genesis app.


### Step 1: Write a one-page premise


Name the player's role, their goal, the setting, the tone and one twist. Keep it to one page. A short premise keeps the AI and your co-writers aligned. Draft it with the free[game world generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-world) , then cut it down by hand.


### Step 2: Build a cast with goals and secrets


Give every major character a goal, a secret and one thing they want from the player. Characters with secrets create choices the player cares about. If you want an AI helper that stays inside one workspace, the[Interactive Story Creator](https://www.taskade.com/agents/creativity/interactive-story-creator) agent template is a single agent, so it fits the Free plan's 1-agent limit.


### Step 3: Map the branches before you write scenes


Sketch three acts, two choices per beat and three endings: one good, one bad and one strange. Draw the map first, because rewriting a map takes minutes and rewriting fifty scenes takes days. The[Branching Scenario Maker](https://www.taskade.com/apps/all/branching-scenario-maker-50hh8l2io7ya2u6t) kit shows one way to store scenes, choices and outcomes.


### Step 4: Choose the build path


- **Authored fiction:** Twine or ink. You write every branch, and you keep every right.
- **A visual novel:** Ren'Py, or Rosebud AI if you want to start from a prompt.
- **Open play:** an AI game master platform such as AI Dungeon or Friends & Fables, with your premise as a custom scenario.
- **A live app with an AI narrator:** Taskade Genesis, described in the next section.


### Step 5: Playtest with three people, then publish


Watch three players run the story. Log where they get stuck, which choices lead to the same place, and which characters appear once and never again. Cut the dead branches. Then publish: itch.io for Twine and Ren'Py, Choice of Games for ChoiceScript, or a share link for a Taskade Genesis app.

## Five Prompts to Run a Story Game in Any AI Assistant


**A clear game-master prompt turns any free AI assistant into a usable text adventure.** These five prompts cover the common jobs: running a game, writing a branching story, exporting to Twine, carrying memory between sessions and playtesting. Paste each one as your first message.


**1. Game master with rules.** Use this when you want the AI to track your state and stop making your choices for you.


```text
You are the game master of a dark fantasy text adventure. I play a disgraced knight. Keep a short status block after every reply: health, inventory, location, open quests. Never decide my actions. End each reply with a question about what I do next.


```


**2. Branching story author.** Use this to get a complete choose-your-own-adventure story you can read or rebuild in an engine.


```text
Write a choose-your-own-adventure story in 12 short scenes. Each scene ends with two choices. Number every scene and say which scene each choice leads to. Include three endings: one good, one bad, one strange.


```


**3. Twine-ready output.** Use this after prompt 2 to paste the story straight into Twine's Harlowe format.


```text
Convert this outline into Twine Harlowe passages. Use [[link]] syntax for each choice. Keep each passage under 120 words.


```


**4. Story so far summary.** Use this at the end of a session. Paste the result at the start of the next one, or into a story card or lorebook.


```text
Summarize our adventure so far in one paragraph, then list every named character, item and promise I made. I will paste this at the start of the next session.


```


**5. Playtest pass.** Use this before you publish. It finds the problems three human testers would find, faster.


```text
Read this branching story and list every dead end, every choice that leads to the same place, and every character who appears once and never again.


```


Results vary by assistant and by plan, so treat the first output as a draft. The[writing prompt generators](https://www.taskade.com/blog/writing-prompt-generators) guide has more story starters if you need a premise.

## From Colossal Cave to AI Game Masters: A Short History


**AI story games are the newest branch of a 50-year line that started with Colossal Cave Adventure in 1976.** Each step changed who writes the story: first programmers, then studios, then writers with free tools, and now a language model that writes the next room on demand.


Year Milestone What it changed


1976 Will Crowther finishes Colossal Cave Adventure on a PDP-10 A story you play by typing commands


1977 Don Woods expands Adventure, and an MIT team starts Zork Richer parsers, puzzles and worlds


1979 to 1980 Infocom is founded, and Zork I ships commercially in December 1980 Interactive fiction becomes a business


2004 Tom Rothamel releases Ren'Py A free engine for visual novels


2009 Twine is released, and Choice of Games launches Choice of the Dragon Free authoring and a publishing path for writers


2014 inkle ships 80 Days, written in its ink language Narrative scripting inside commercial games


2019 AI Dungeon 2 launches in December on GPT-2 The AI writes the branch on demand


2025 Story2Game paper describes generated actions grounded in world state Research on keeping AI stories playable


2026 inkle releases TR-49, and AI Dungeon opens Voyage to everyone Authored and AI-driven story games grow side by side

Zork I sold 380,000 copies by 1986, according to its Wikipedia history. Text adventures then faded from stores for two decades, and writers kept the form alive with free tools. Twine games such as Howling Dogs and Depression Quest reached wide audiences in the early 2010s, and Charlie Brooker used Twine while he developed Black Mirror: Bandersnatch.

The lesson from text adventures applies to any story you tell, as our[storytelling lessons from text adventures](https://www.taskade.com/blog/startup-storytelling) post argues: a player stays when every room promises something new and every choice has a consequence.

## Where AI Story Games Still Fall Short


**AI story games in 2026 still struggle with three things: long-term consistency, fair rules and endings.** A model can write a vivid scene, but it does not know where the story should go unless someone told it. These limits are worth knowing before you pay for any plan.


- **Consistency over hundreds of turns.** Every tool in the play group forgets eventually. Saved facts and structured state slow the drift, but they do not stop it.
- **Fair rules.** Without a rules engine, a persuasive player wins every fight. Friends & Fables answers this with 5e-based combat. Chat assistants leave it to you.
- **Endings.** Open-ended games rarely end on their own. Authored engines end where the writer decided, which is why Twine, ink and Ren'Py still produce the most memorable story games.
- **Rights and prices that change.** Several platforms publish no price or ownership terms on a public page. Check before you build a long project on one.


The pattern points at a mixed approach. Write the world, the cast and the endings yourself, then let the AI improvise inside them. That is how the strongest tools in each group already work.

## AI Story Game FAQ


What is the best AI story game in 2026?


It depends on what you want at the end of the evening. For an open-ended text adventure, AI Dungeon has the largest community library. For a campaign with real rules, Friends & Fables runs an AI game master with tactical combat based on D&D 5e rules. For stories set in famous worlds, try Hidden Door. To publish your own interactive fiction, Twine and ink are free and open source.


What is the best free AI text adventure?


Perchance AI RPG is free with no sign-up and states no daily limit. Friends & Fables gives 25 free game-master turns a day, Altworld starts with 10 guest turns, and AI Dungeon lets you play its base model without paying. ChatGPT and Claude also run a text adventure on their free plans if you give them a game-master prompt. Free plans checked November 7, 2026.


Is AI Dungeon still free in 2026?


Yes. AI Dungeon's pricing FAQ says you can use the model at its base amount endlessly without spending anything, and its Voyage public multiplayer is free for everyone. Paid memberships add a monthly credit allowance and more context. The plan list did not load on November 7, 2026, so we do not quote tier prices here.


Is "Storygame AI" a single app?


No. "Storygame AI" is mostly how people search for the whole category of AI story games. The closest product name is StoryGames.AI, a visual-novel assistant that Buildbox described in a 2023 guide for Buildbox Classic. Its current availability is not confirmed. Most people who search the term want an AI game master such as AI Dungeon or Friends & Fables.


How do AI story games work?


You type what your character does. The AI reads your action, the recent story and any saved facts, such as story cards or a lorebook, then writes the next scene. Some platforms also run a rules check, such as a combat turn, before they narrate. Authored tools such as Twine work differently: the writer creates every branch in advance.


Why do AI story games forget things?


A language model sees only a limited amount of recent text, so early details fall out of view in a long run. Story cards, lorebooks, long-term memories and short summaries help. Pin the facts that matter, and start a new chapter with a one-paragraph recap instead of playing hundreds of turns in one session.


Can I make my own AI story game without coding?


Yes. Twine lets you write branching stories without code and publishes to HTML. Rosebud AI and Gameer turn a description into a playable interactive story. In Taskade, you can describe a story game and Taskade Genesis builds a live web app with scenes, characters and an AI narrator.


Can I sell an interactive fiction game I made?


Often, but read the license first. Twine says anything you create is free to use, including commercially, and Ren'Py is free for commercial use. ChoiceScript is different: its license bars commercial use unless Choice of Games publishes the game or grants a commercial license. Rosebud AI grants commercial rights from its $30 a month 10x Dev plan. Check a hosted platform's terms for your plan before you sell.


Is there an AI dungeon master for D&D?


Yes. Friends & Fables runs an AI game master with tactical turn-based combat based on D&D 5e rules, long-term memories and battlemaps, and its free plan includes 25 turns a day. For a human-run table, Taskade offers a free D&D content generator and a Tabletop Campaign Manager kit for sessions, NPCs and quests. That kit holds automations, so cloning it needs a paid plan.


Are AI story games safe for kids?


Check each platform's age rules first. Character.AI removed open-ended chat for users under 18 in late 2025 and points teens to a guided Stories format instead. Hidden Door rates each world's content, from All ages to Mature. Authored tools such as Twine involve no live AI at all, so a parent or teacher controls every word of the story.


Can Taskade make an AI story game?


Yes, as a web app. Taskade Genesis builds a story game from a prompt, with scenes and characters stored as projects and an AI agent as the narrator. Taskade is not a combat-rules game master like Friends & Fables. It is strongest for the story bible, the branch map and a shareable story app.


Do I need a paid plan to build a story game in Taskade?


You can start on Free, which includes 3 Taskade Genesis apps, 1 AI agent, 10 automation runs per billing period and 2 workspace members. Free starts with 0 AI credits. On Free, you earn free AI credits with referrals and invites, and you can upgrade any time. A kit that holds automations, such as the AI Story Game kit, needs a paid plan to clone. Pro is $10 a month billed annually.

## The Verdict


For open play, **AI Dungeon** is still the default, and **Perchance** is the free way to try the genre. For rules and a group, **Friends & Fables** runs the most complete AI game master. For known worlds, **Hidden Door** . For prose, **NovelAI** . For authored fiction, **Twine** and **ink** , and for a visual novel you can sell, **Ren'Py** .


And before any of them, write the world down. The play platforms improvise well, but they improvise best inside a world, a cast and an ending someone wrote first.
